title: Guided free-form picking
thesis: With Level Up mode off, the level control shows a working level beside the character's level — the next empty pick slot, or a clicked one — powers out of reach at the working level are dimmed but still pickable, an empty pick slot can be clicked to target it, and a power held without its prerequisite at an earlier level is marked until the build is put back in order.
body:
Free-form (Level Up mode off) is the default and stays free: nothing is refused for being early
or out of order. It guides instead, the way Mids' Reborn does outside its own level-up mode.
Level Up mode stays the strict option and is not changed by this work.

Decisions (2026-10-10, user-chosen):
- The level that follows the picks is a separate *working level*, shown beside the character's
  level as `50 (14)`. `CharacterState::level` stays what the user set and still drives totals,
  slot budget and inherents. The working level drives only dimming and where the next pick goes.
  Once every pick is filled the control shows just `50`.
  Rejected: moving `CharacterState::level` itself (chosen earlier the same day, then replaced by
  the user — totals and the slot budget would shift with every pick).
- The working level is computed from the build (earliest empty pick slot), so it is not saved
  and adds no undo steps. Only a clicked slot is held, as temporary UI state.
- A pick above the current level lands in the earliest empty slot it can legally fill. This is
  already what `next_pick_level` does.
- Prerequisites come from the power's `requires` expression in the contract, the same data that
  gates picks today. No hand-written table.
- Only a missing or out-of-order prerequisite raises the warning. It shows in two places: on the
  power's card in the by-level grid, and as a red italic name in the power list (Mids shows only
  the latter).
- Clicking an empty pick slot sets the working level to that slot's level (Mids' behaviour).
  After the next pick it returns to the earliest empty slot.
- Level Up mode keeps refusing a pick whose prerequisite is missing.

## Preconditions

- `main` builds and `cargo nextest run --workspace` passes before work starts.
- The homecoming contract carries `requires` on pool powers — checked 2026-10-10:
  `Pool.Fighting.Tough` has `["Pool.Fighting.Boxing","Pool.Fighting.Kick","||"]`.

## Out of scope

- The by-powerset layout of the Powers panel: it has no empty slots to click. The working level
  still shows there (guided-picking-3).
- Any change to Level Up mode beyond keeping its refusal (guided-picking-2).
- Fixing an out-of-order build automatically. The planner marks it; the user reorders.
- Any change to how `CharacterState::level` is set. The user's level control works as before.
- Order checks on enhancement slot levels. This plan is about power picks only.
- Set-level gates (`PoolDef.buy_requires`, epic `minLevel`): they are level rules, which
  placement already honours.

says: an order-aware prerequisite check in `coh_data::pick_rules`: for a held power, the prerequisite counts only if it is held at a strictly lower pick level.
body:
Today
`requires_met` counts ownership at any level.
Done 2026-10-10 as `requires_met_in_order`, which evaluates the power's own `requires`
against the build with every pick at or above its level removed. Mutation-checked: with
the old any-level behaviour, two of the four tests fail.
verify: fn:requires_met_in_order, file:crates/coh_data/tests/prerequisite_order.rs

says: with Level Up mode off, a power whose gate is `PickGate::Closed` is pickable and lands at `next_pick_level`.
body:
With Level Up mode on it is still refused.
Done 2026-10-10. Narrowed on the way: only a gate that an earlier pick from the power's
own set would open (`PickGate::NeedsEarlier`, via `requires_met_with_set`) is let through.
Exclusion locks and archetype gates stay `Closed` and refused in both modes — reordering
can never fix those. Q/A on the web build: Tzarina (Homecoming) took Tough with no
Boxing or Kick and it landed at L30; with Level Up mode on, Tough was refused.
verify: fn:requires_met_with_set, fn:row_verdict, fn:commit_blocker

says: a working level, computed as the earliest empty pick slot (or the clicked slot, guided-picking-5), shown in the level control as `50 (14)` when Level Up mode is off and a pick is still empty.
body:
`CharacterState::level` is never changed by it.
Done 2026-10-10 as `level_control::working_level`. It replaces the old "Next pick Lvl N"
readout beside Level Up and the phone bar's "Next" chip, which showed the same number by
the same rule (decision 2026-10-10, Claude's call — one number in one place). The clicked
slot override arrives with guided-picking-5. Q/A on the web build: Tzarina read `28 (30)`, `28 (32)`
after taking Tough, `28` with Level Up mode on; Charnel (all picks filled) read `50`; the
Pixel 7 phone bar read `28 (30)` and fit.
verify: fn:working_level, file:crates/coh_data/tests/working_level.rs

says: power-list rows that unlock above the working level are dimmed as a whole row, not just the badge tint `is-locked` gives today, and stay clickable.
body:
Done 2026-10-10 via `level_control::reach_level` (working level in free-form, the
character's level in Level Up mode or once every pick is filled), read by the Available
rows and the pool picker's rows alike. Hover lifts a dimmed row to full ink. Q/A on the
web build with Tzarina's first three picks at level 50: the control read `50 (4)`; Water
Blast and Cold Domination rows at 2 and 4 were bright, 6 and up dimmed; clicking the dimmed
Geyser took it at 26; in the pool picker Boxing and Kick (4) were bright, the 14s dimmed.
The plan named Archery; Water Blast stood in, the same check on a set a fixture holds.
verify: fn:reach_level

says: an empty cell in the by-level grid (`PowersByLevel`) can be clicked.
body:
The click
sets the working level to that cell's level and highlights the cell. The next pick fills that cell
if the power is legal there, otherwise the earliest legal empty slot.
Done 2026-10-10. Placement is `LevelingSchedule::pick_level_toward`; the clicked slot is
`level_control::TargetSlot`, UI state cleared by the next pick from either picker.
Clicking the aimed cell again lets go. The working slot is highlighted as "Next pick"
even before any click (Claude's call — the grid then always says where the next power
goes). Level Up mode keeps the cells plain and ignores the target. Q/A on the web build:
aimed L24 → `50 (24)`; Aqua Bolt landed at 24 and the control returned to `50 (4)`;
aimed L18, Geyser landed at 26; the second click on L20 let go; Pixel 7 tap aimed L24.
verify: fn:pick_level_toward, fn:TargetSlot, file:crates/coh_data/tests/working_level.rs

says: a power held without its prerequisite at an earlier level (guided-picking-1) is marked on its grid card and shown red italic in the power list.
body:
The tooltip names what is missing
("needs Boxing or Kick at an earlier level"). Both clear once the build is back in order.
Done 2026-10-10 as `powers::out_of_order_reason`, worded by `prerequisite_phrase`: a
choice reads "Boxing or Kick", a richer rule (Weave's two of three) reads "enough of
Boxing, Kick and Tough" rather than restating it. The card mark is a small red `!` after
the name, on the card both Powers layouts share. Shown in either mode: a loaded build can
be out of order with Level Up on. Q/A on the web build: Tough alone at 14 showed both
marks, tooltip "Out of order: Tough needs Boxing or Kick picked before level 14"; Kick
added at 4 cleared both; Kick given back and re-taken into the clicked L20 slot brought
both back.
verify: fn:out_of_order_reason, fn:prerequisite_phrase

says: Q/A pass in the web build with screenshots (`qa-check` skill), Level Up mode off, covering: a level-1 build picked in order, an out-of-level pick, a slot click, the Tough case, and Level Up mode still refusing Tough.
body:
Done 2026-10-10 on `main` after the merge, Tzarina's two level-1 picks as the start:
in order, the control read `50 (2)` → `(4)` → `(6)` → `(8)` and the dimming followed;
Geyser (dimmed) landed at 26 with the control held at `(8)`; aiming L24 read `50 (24)`
and Aqua Bolt landed there, back to `(8)`; Tough alone was marked, Kick at 8 cleared it,
Kick moved to 28 brought it back; Level Up mode refused Tough. The pass found the pool
picker's row still drawn as free-form's "take it early" in Level Up mode, fixed to read
as refused there. Console clean.

says: A Mids .mbd or .mxd import keeps the level the file places each slot at, instead of packing every slot at the earliest grant.
body: Reported by a user 2026-10-14: loading a previous build shows slot levels filled in lowest-possible rather than where they put them. Mids writes a Level on every SlotEntry; mbd_import::to_skif_build never wrote slot_order, so slot_levels solved an empty history and packed every slot. Beta seeded it in seedSlotOrderFromFile (its MBDEXPORT-18). Native saves (localStorage, .skif) already round-trip slot_order and are not affected. .mxd goes through the same to_skif_build, so one fix covers both.

evidence: mbd_import::seed_slot_order writes each placed slot's file level into slot_order as Authored. build_file::tests::mbd_import_keeps_the_files_slot_levels compares every paired slot of the Homecoming Blaster .mbd fixture to the file and fails with the seed call removed (Tranquilizer_Dart slot 1: 5 vs 3). Full nextest 232/232, clippy and fmt clean. In the web app the same file shows Combat Jumping 8/17/27/29 and Gymnastics 24/46/50/50/50 (Mids' 47s, which Homecoming never grants, moved to 50).

title: Layout follows the account
thesis: A signed-in player's layout is saved to their account automatically and comes back on any browser or device they sign in on, the most recently edited copy winning, while a signed-out player sees no change at all.
body:
Player feedback, 2026-10-01: building a dashboard is many clicks and drags, and it is lost
on a new browser, a new device, or a cleared cache. Today every part of the layout lives only
in that browser's `localStorage`. The live site was checked the same day: a layout does
survive a reload, so the loss is where it is kept, not a save bug.

"Layout" here means exactly five stored keys, no more:

| key | what it holds | written by |
|---|---|---|
| `sk-stats-config` | the stat panels, their names and their stats | [stats_store.rs](../crates/app/src/stats_store.rs) |
| `sk-layout` | each panel's place on the desktop grid, one slot per column count | [layout_store.rs](../crates/app/src/layout_store.rs) |
| `sk-mobile-order` | the order of panels on a phone | [layout_store.rs](../crates/app/src/layout_store.rs) |
| `sk-quickbar` | the pinned quickbar buttons | [layout_store.rs](../crates/app/src/layout_store.rs) |
| `sk-powers-layout` | the Powers panel's by-powerset / by-level view | [layout_store.rs](../crates/app/src/layout_store.rs) |

Decisions, 2026-10-01, user-chosen:

- **Layout only.** Rejected: also theme, UI size and alert settings (more to test, and UI
  size arguably belongs to the device); stat panels only (grid positions would still be lost).
- **Newest edit wins**, whole layout against whole layout. Rejected: account always wins
  (overwrites a layout built before signing in, silently); asking the player (a dialog to
  design for a case the timestamp already answers).
  Amended 2026-10-01 after the first signed-in test (user-chosen): newest wins only between
  copies of the same account's layout. A layout edited signed out, or under another account,
  loses to the account's copy at sign-in, and an account with no copy yet takes the browser's.
  Found when panels hidden while signed out overwrote the account's copy on signing back in.
- **Saved automatically**, a moment after the last change. Rejected: a save button
  (players forget, which is the failure being fixed).

The server is the Supabase project the beta also uses. Its schema lives in the beta's repo,
`~/Github/CoH-Sidekick/supabase/schema.sql`, and changes reach the live database as a
migration file pasted into the SQL editor. The `favorites` table (schema.sql:517) is the
pattern: one user's rows, readable and writable only by that user, written straight from the
client with no edge function.

## Preconditions

Checked 2026-10-01:

- The beta repo `~/Github/CoH-Sidekick` has a clean working tree.
- The client can already select and upsert table rows: `Cloud::select` and `Cloud::upsert`
  in [cloud/mod.rs](../crates/app/src/cloud/mod.rs).
- Sign-in already triggers a per-user fetch (favorites) at
  [account.rs:261](../crates/app/src/cloud/account.rs#L261), which is where the layout
  fetch joins.

Not checkable from here, and assumed: sign-in works on next.coh-sidekick.com and in the
desktop build, and the live database matches `schema.sql`.

## Out of scope

- **Theme, UI size, alerts and other display preferences.** Decided out above; a later plan
  can add keys to the same document once this one works.
- **Live sync between two open tabs.** The other tab picks up the change on its next load.
  Pushing changes into an open page is a separate, larger feature.
- **Merging two layouts.** Newest wins whole. A merge has no right answer for a panel moved
  in both copies.
- **The build itself (`sk-build`).** Builds already save to the account their own way.
- **Layout history or undo.** One copy per account.
- **The beta reading this table.** It is written for this app; the beta never sees it.

says: a `user_layouts` table: one row per user holding the layout as one JSON document plus the time it was last edited, readable and writable only by its owner, with a size cap.
body:
Added to the beta's `schema.sql`, with
`supabase/migration-2026-10-01-user-layouts.sql` beside it. Done 2026-10-01: the
beta's supabase tests pass (182, four new in `schema-access.test.ts`); the migration
applied twice to the Docker fixture without error and kept its rows; and
`supabase/audit/fixture/check-user-layouts.sql` executed every access case (own
read/write allowed; another account's row, delete, anon and oversize all refused).

says: the migration is applied to the live database.
body:
needs: layout-sync-1
Done 2026-10-01: the user ran it in the SQL editor; an anonymous REST read of
`user_layouts` answers `42501 permission denied`, where a missing table answers
`PGRST205`, so the table is live and anon is refused.

says: the browser records when its layout was last changed, and the five keys can be read out and written back as one document.
body:
A layout that has never been edited
has no time, so any account copy beats it. Done 2026-10-01 in
[layout_sync.rs](../crates/app/src/layout_sync.rs): an edit is a write that changes a
key's content after the first pointer or key press, so the app's own writes while it
loads never date the layout. Checked in a browser: a fresh load and dismissing the
welcome window left no time; folding a panel stamped one; a reload left it unchanged.
verify: fn:commit_tracked, tests:layout_sync>=6

says: upload: while signed in, any layout change is sent to the account a couple of seconds after the last one.
body:
needs: layout-sync-2, layout-sync-3
Done 2026-10-01, checked by the user on next.coh-sidekick.com: a burst of edits made one
upload, and the row's `edited_at` matched the last edit within seconds.

says: download: on sign-in and on page load while signed in, the newer of the two copies wins.
body:
An account copy that wins is applied to the screen without a reload,
and a browser copy that wins is uploaded.   needs: layout-sync-2, layout-sync-3
Done 2026-10-01, checked by the user: a layout made in one browser appeared in a private
window after signing in, and an edit there appeared back in the first browser on reload.
Two defects found on the way, both fixed the same day: a layout edited signed out
overwrote the account's (the amended rule under the decisions above), and a layout read
back from the account failed to parse because `jsonb` reorders keys, so the default
showed on every load (`parse_desktop` in [layout_store.rs](../crates/app/src/layout_store.rs)).

says: signed out, offline or server error: nothing changes from today.
body:
The
browser copy always saves, and a failed upload is retried on the next change rather
than reported on every drag.   needs: layout-sync-4, layout-sync-5
@unchecked done when: signed out, editing and reloading behaves as before; signed in
with the Supabase address blocked in devtools, editing and reloading still keeps the
layout and shows no error popups.

says: the desktop app syncs too, through the same code.
